desc: Indian engineering company in the Kalyani Group making forged and machined components for cars, trucks, aerospace, energy and defence.
markets: Plants in India, Europe and the United States supply vehicle, energy and defence customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B forging company with international footprint and Indian brand; technology tie-in exists but F1 fit is moderate.

name: CDB Aviation
desc: Dublin-based aircraft lessor owning and leasing commercial passenger aircraft to airlines worldwide, wholly owned by China Development Bank Financial Leasing.
markets: Leases aircraft to airlines worldwide; owned by Chinese state-bank-linked lessor CDB Financial Leasing.
rationale: B2B lessor with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could suit airline clients, but fit is weak.

name: ICEYE
desc: Finnish space company operating small radar imaging satellites, selling imagery and analytics to government and commercial customers.
markets: Sells satellite imagery to defence, insurance, disaster response and commercial customers in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Space data company with technology showcase value but defence-heavy customers and little consumer marketing; modest F1 fit.

name: Castelion
desc: Defence technology start-up developing hypersonic weapons for the US military, notably the Blackbeard missile for the Army.
markets: Customers are US military services; founded in 2022 with no known commercial or international markets.
rationale: Weapons developer with government customers and no consumer brand; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: Dassault Systemes
desc: French software company selling 3D design, simulation and product lifecycle management software, including CATIA, SOLIDWORKS and SIMULIA.
markets: Enterprise customers in automotive, aerospace, industrial and life-sciences sectors across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Engineering software brand with strong motorsport design and simulation tie-in, global enterprise customers and B2B hospitality value.

name: Firefly Aerospace
desc: Space company building Alpha launch vehicles, the Blue Ghost lunar lander and Elytra orbital vehicles for government and commercial customers.
markets: Customers include NASA and US commercial and defence buyers; Blue Ghost landed on the Moon in March 2025.
rationale: Space start-up with little consumer brand and mainly US government customers; F1 fit is weak.

name: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP)
desc: Airport operator holding concessions for 12 Mexican Pacific airports, including Guadalajara, Tijuana and Los Cabos, plus airports in Jamaica.
markets: Airports in Mexico and Jamaica serving leisure and business passengers.
rationale: Airport group tied to Mexican and Caribbean tourism; Mexico Grand Prix gives some visibility, but marketing is limited.

name: HEICO Corporation
desc: Aerospace, defence and electronics company known for FAA-approved replacement parts for aircraft engines and airframes used by airlines.
markets: Sells parts and electronics to airlines, aircraft makers and defence customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B parts supplier with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality is possible, but marketing culture is minimal.

name: Hexcel Corporation
desc: Maker of advanced composites such as carbon fibre, prepregs and honeycomb used in aircraft including the A350 and Boeing 787.
markets: Supplies aircraft makers and industrial customers worldwide with plants in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Composites supplier with materials-technology tie-in to motorsport lightweighting, but a B2B profile with limited consumer marketing.

name: Impulse Space
desc: Builder of orbital transfer vehicles and propulsion, such as Mira and Helios, moving satellites from launch drop-off to final orbit.
markets: Customers are US government and commercial satellite operators; founded in 2021 by a SpaceX founding engineer.
rationale: Young space propulsion company with no consumer brand and mainly government and satellite customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Isar Aerospace
desc: German launch company developing the Spectrum two-stage rocket to put small and medium satellites into orbit from Andoya, Norway.
markets: Based near Munich with launches from Norway; pre-revenue after a first launch attempt in March 2025.
rationale: Pre-revenue rocket developer with no consumer brand; German base offers a technology story but weak F1 fit.

name: Redwire
desc: Space infrastructure company making solar arrays, deployable structures, sensors and in-space manufacturing systems, and owner of Edge Autonomy.
markets: Sells to NASA, defence and commercial space customers in the United States and Europe.
rationale: Space and defence supplier with little consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite technology story.
changed: Acquired Edge Autonomy in 2025

name: Vertical Aerospace
desc: British developer of the VX4 battery-electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft for air taxi use, founded by Ovo Energy's founder.
markets: Pre-revenue aircraft developer based in the United Kingdom, with pre-orders from airlines and lessors.
rationale: UK electric-aircraft start-up with a sustainability story, but pre-revenue, so F1 fit is limited.

name: Voyager Technologies
desc: Defence and space technology company supplying satellites, propulsion, defence electronics and commercial space station services including the Starlab programme.
markets: Customers are mainly US defence and space agencies; international partners exist through the Starlab station project.
rationale: Defence-led space supplier with little consumer brand and mostly government customers; F1 fit is weak.

name: Vulcan Elements
desc: Manufacturer of rare-earth permanent magnets building US domestic magnet production for aerospace, defence, electric vehicle and industrial customers.
markets: Customers are US aerospace, defence, EV and industrial buyers; aims to reduce reliance on Chinese magnets.
rationale: Young US magnet maker with no consumer brand; EV technology link exists but F1 fit is weak.

name: Airbus
desc: European aerospace and defence manufacturer building A320, A350 and A380 airliners, helicopters, military aircraft and space systems.
markets: Sells to airlines and governments worldwide, with main operations in Toulouse, Hamburg and Seville.
rationale: Global aerospace brand with B2B hospitality and technology showcase value, and strong European airline customers.

name: Axiom Space
desc: Space company running private astronaut missions to the International Space Station, building commercial station modules and spacesuits for NASA.
industry: private astronaut missions and space stations
markets: Sells missions to private individuals and governments from several countries; also works for NASA.
rationale: Brand-led space company with affluent customers and global governments as clients; plausible but not obvious F1 fit.

name: CesiumAstro
desc: Builder of phased array communications payloads and terminals for satellites, aircraft and drones, selling to defence, space and commercial customers.
markets: Customers are mainly US defence, space and commercial buyers; overseas sales not verified.
rationale: Defence and space component supplier with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Chang Guang Satellite Technology
desc: Chinese commercial remote-sensing satellite company operating the Jilin-1 constellation that supplies imagery to farming, mapping and government customers.
markets: Operates from Changchun, supplying imagery mainly to Chinese customers; spun out of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
rationale: State-linked Chinese imaging firm with no consumer brand; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: Eve Air Mobility
desc: Urban air mobility company developing an electric air taxi, with air traffic software and services, majority-owned by Embraer.
markets: Development in Florida and Brazil with letters of intent from operators in several regions; no commercial service yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue air taxi developer backed by Embraer, with limited consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Falcata
desc: Arlington defence technology company providing engineering and systems to defence customers; further details are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Virginia, serving defence customers; markets beyond that are not confirmed.
rationale: Defence-focused company with no known consumer brand or marketing activity; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: GA Telesis
desc: Commercial aviation company providing aircraft engine and component leasing, parts distribution, maintenance and aircraft teardown services to airlines and lessors.
markets: Founded in 1996; sells to airlines and lessors in several regions.
rationale: B2B aviation parts and leasing firm with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: K2 Space
desc: Builder of large high-power satellite platforms, designed for launch on Starship and other rockets, for government and commercial customers.
markets: Founded in 2022 by former SpaceX engineers; customers are mainly US government and commercial operators.
rationale: Space start-up building satellite platforms for government customers, with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Larsen & Toubro
desc: Indian engineering and construction conglomerate building infrastructure, power plants, hydrocarbon projects and defence equipment, with IT services through subsidiaries.
markets: Projects in India, the Middle East, Africa and other regions; IT services serve clients in North America and Europe.
rationale: Large Indian industrial brand with Gulf and global projects; B2B hospitality value, but F1 consumer fit is limited.

name: Mach Industries
desc: Defence manufacturer building autonomous drones and munitions, such as the Viper Strike glide weapon, for US and allied customers.
markets: Founded in 2023; customers are US and allied defence buyers.
rationale: Weapons-focused defence start-up with no consumer brand and government customers; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: Planet Labs
desc: Operator of a large fleet of Earth imaging satellites selling daily imagery and analytics subscriptions to government and commercial customers.
markets: Customers in agriculture, finance, mapping and government across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Data and space brand with technology showcase appeal, but mainly B2B and government buyers; modest F1 fit.

name: True Anomaly
desc: Space security company building Jackal autonomous orbital vehicles for space domain awareness and rendezvous and proximity operations.
markets: Founded in 2022 by former US Space Force officers; customers are mainly the US government.
rationale: Defence-oriented space start-up with no consumer brand and mainly government customers; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: DISH Network
desc: US pay-TV and wireless company with DISH satellite TV, Sling TV streaming and Boost Mobile, serving American households and subscribers.
markets: Customers are US households and mobile subscribers; no international operations.
rationale: Large US consumer media and wireless brand, but US-only, so F1 value is limited to American fan reach.
changed: Merged with EchoStar in 2023

name: We Energies
desc: Trade name of Wisconsin Electric Power Company, a regulated utility supplying electricity and natural gas in Wisconsin.
markets: Serves about one million customers each for electricity and gas in Wisconsin; no operations abroad.
rationale: Regional regulated utility with local customers only and no marketing need; weak F1 fit.

name: Aena
desc: Spanish airport operator managing 46 airports in Spain and holding stakes in airports abroad, including London Luton and Brazil.
markets: Airports in Spain, the United Kingdom, Brazil and other countries; state-controlled and listed in Madrid.
rationale: Large airport operator with Spain's Madrid Grand Prix on the calendar and passenger reach; B2B hospitality and travel-retail angle.

name: Air India
desc: India's flag carrier operating domestic and international passenger flights, part of the Tata Group and merged with Vistara in 2024.
markets: Network across India and to North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Large consumer airline with international premium travellers and a growing Indian F1 audience; strong brand and hospitality fit.
changed: Returned to Tata Group in 2022; merged with Vistara in 2024
f1: Part-owned (25.1%) by Singapore Airlines, a current F1 partner; Air India itself is not a partner
